user_intent: A single wide split-frame image making a visual argument about who learning spaces are actually built for. Left half: a traditional institutional classroom — rows of fixed desks, cold fluorescent overhead lighting, two elementary students sitting rigidly and passively. Right half: a modern flexible learning environment — warm natural light from large windows, flexible furniture, the same two students now leaning in, active, and engaged. A clear architectural or lighting transition divides the two worlds. No text. The image argues by contrast alone.

subject.description: Elementary school student, approximately 10 years old, Black girl with hair in two puffs, wearing a light blue t-shirt and dark pants. Seated rigidly at a fixed individual desk in a row, spine straight against an uncomfortable hard chair, hands folded flat on the empty desk surface, eyes forward or downward, expression blank and uninspired — the posture of endurance, not engagement.
subject.pose: sitting rigidly upright at a fixed desk, hands flat on empty desk surface, looking forward or down, shoulders slightly slumped, no materials in front of her

subject.description: Elementary school student, approximately 10 years old, white boy with light brown hair, wearing a gray t-shirt and dark jeans. Seated at a fixed desk in the same institutional row, slumped slightly, chin resting on one hand, looking forward with a blank unfocused expression — bored, waiting, enduring.
subject.pose: seated at fixed desk, chin resting on one hand propped on the desk, elbow on desk surface, eyes forward but unfocused, other arm limp

subject.description: The same Black girl with hair in two puffs, same light blue t-shirt — now on the right side of the frame, completely transformed in body language. Leaning forward over a flexible collaborative table, both hands actively working with project materials, head tilted toward a classmate, expression alive with focus and curiosity.
subject.pose: leaning forward over a flexible table, both hands engaged with project materials, slightly turned toward student_B_right, expression fully engaged

subject.description: The same white boy with light brown hair, same gray t-shirt — now on the right side of the frame, completely transformed. Sitting forward at the edge of a flexible chair, pointing at something on the work surface with one hand, mouth slightly open mid-sentence, eyes bright and focused.
subject.pose: sitting forward at the edge of a flexible chair, one hand pointing at materials on the table, body turned slightly toward student_A_right, mouth open mid-conversation

scene.location: A single wide space that transitions visibly from a traditional institutional classroom on the left to a modern flexible learning environment on the right — two worlds occupying one frame, separated by a clear architectural divide.

lighting.left_half: cold flat overhead fluorescent lighting — pale, even, institutional, no shadows, no warmth
lighting.right_half: warm natural sunlight streaming in from large windows on the right wall — golden, directional, alive

background_elements_left: rows of identical fixed individual desks with hard plastic chairs attached
chalkboard or whiteboard at the front — empty
no windows visible on the left side
uniform desk spacing communicating control and sameness
no materials on desk surfaces — empty, waiting
background_elements_right: modern flexible collaborative tables with rounded edges in warm wood tone
upholstered moveable chairs in muted blues and greens
large floor-to-ceiling windows flooding the right side with warm natural light
project materials — paper, markers, small models — on the table surface
open sightlines suggesting a larger purposeful space beyond
warm wood flooring, clean architectural ceiling elements
scene.dividing_element: A clear visual transition at the horizontal center of the frame — ideally an architectural column, a wall edge, or a sharp shift from cold fluorescent light on the left to warm natural light on the right. The divide should feel real and structural, not composited.

composition.left_half_content: Traditional institutional classroom — rows, fixed desks, cold fluorescent light, passive students. Occupies left 50% of frame.
composition.right_half_content: Modern flexible learning environment — natural light, flexible furniture, same students now active and engaged. Occupies right 50% of frame.

logo_safe_zone.instruction: This region falls on the traditional/institutional side of the split frame. Keep student bodies and faces clear of this corner — empty desk surface or institutional floor is acceptable here. Kay-Twelve logo badge overlay applied in post-processing.

negative_prompt: primary subject in bottom left corner
advanced._note: Negative prompts intentionally omit 'artificial light', 'sterile', and 'catalog style' — the left half of this split-frame intentionally uses fluorescent light and institutional sterility as a visual contrast device.
